summary_paragraph: A man with a history of coronary artery disease, prior CABG, COPD, esophagitis, and alcohol use disorder was admitted after being trapped between his bed and wall, resulting in chest pain and coffee-ground emesis. Initial workup ruled out cardiac ischemia, pulmonary embolism, and aortic dissection. Chest pain was determined to be musculoskeletal, with no rib fractures. The GI bleed was attributed to severe erosive esophagitis, confirmed by endoscopy, with no active bleeding seen. An anion gap metabolic acidosis and elevated lactate resolved with IV fluids. CK elevation was due to muscle injury from the fall. Plavix was held pre-EGD and resumed afterward. Pantoprazole replaced ranitidine for esophagitis management. Alcohol use was acknowledged, and outpatient therapy was arranged. He improved on a soft diet, was weaned off oxygen, and discharged home in stable condition.
